memory_update.text: MIDD is the reference public leader for restaurant commercial kitchen, refrigeration, beverage, IoT, and automation equipment in this node.
WSO is a non-obvious refrigeration/HVAC distributor candidate; restaurant exposure is likely hidden within commercial refrigeration and contractor demand rather than directly disclosed.
WEST is a small-cap beverage-solutions candidate for restaurant beverage complexity, but equipment-service exposure remains unverified.
PFGC is a speculative-shadow broadline distributor candidate because kitchen equipment and restaurant supplies are offered through Performance Foodservice, but materiality is not disclosed.

Farmer Brothers appears highly relevant to coffee-equipment service and DSD but should be removed from active US-listed universe tracking after its May 5, 2026 take-private closing unless a public listing reappears.

Need a focused follow-up search for public pure-play commercial kitchen service networks, OEM parts distributors, ice-machine/refrigeration service platforms, and beverage-dispensing service firms; many likely private or buried inside conglomerates.

FARM is the strongest underfollowed fit for the beverage-machine service lane because provided evidence explicitly mentions foodservice customers and coffee-machine sales/service, but market-cap/liquidity and financial health may make it a speculative exception.

WEST belongs in the beverage-complexity lane as a B2B coffee/tea/extract supplier to foodservice operators, but its inclusion in the equipment-service node should be conditional on finding dispensing-system or field-service evidence.

Restaurant equipment/service chokepoints may split into three subnodes for later layers: commercial kitchen OEMs, beverage/coffee route-service providers, and regulated refrigeration inputs/service networks.

Need official filing evidence for MIDD aftermarket/service revenue, FARM equipment service economics, WEST dispensing/equipment support, and HDSN commercial refrigeration end-market exposure before any candidate survives Layer 2.
MIDD is the cleanest US-listed reference asset for commercial restaurant equipment and aftermarket/service exposure, but not an underfollowed small-cap.
FARM is a high-relevance but high-risk micro-cap exception: direct coffee/beverage equipment installation, repair, refurbishment, and DSD service network.
WEST belongs in the beverage-complexity second-order lane, but equipment-maintenance exposure is unverified and should not be upgraded without customer/service evidence.

Many pure-play restaurant equipment service networks, parts distributors, Taylor/Henny Penny/Franke service territories, and CFESA repair platforms appear private or non-US-listed; this limits clean public-market mapping.
The service bottleneck may be more about installed-base uptime, factory-certified technicians, parts availability, warranties, and preventative maintenance than new equipment sales alone.
MIDD should remain the reference benchmark for restaurant commercial equipment, especially cooking, refrigeration, beverage dispensing, and integrated kitchen systems.

FARM is a speculative micro-cap discovery candidate for coffee/beverage supply plus possible equipment service, but the thesis requires verification of machine service revenue, DSD economics, and customer concentration.
HBB is a speculative shadow candidate where commercial foodservice appliances may be hidden inside a broader consumer appliance label.

HDSN maps to the adjacent refrigeration uptime chokepoint rather than direct restaurant equipment; regulatory refrigerant constraints may make the exposure more relevant than standard industry labels suggest.

Need a later pass on private or acquired companies such as Parts Town, Smart Care, Ali Group/Welbilt, and beverage equipment service networks to identify public suppliers, lenders, distributors, or spinout possibilities.

node: Restaurant equipment, beverage-machine service, maintenance, and field support
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the public-company universe for the restaurant equipment/service/beverage-machine node. The cleanest direct public leader is Middleby, while Watsco is a less obvious second-order refrigeration/HVAC distribution exposure. Westrock Coffee is a small-cap beverage-supply-chain platform with foodservice and restaurant exposure but needs verification for installed-equipment/service economics. Performance Food Group is included as a broadline restaurant distribution/customer-access platform that touches kitchen equipment and supplies, but the maintenance/service chokepoint linkage is weaker. Farmer Brothers would have been a strong small-cap evidence candidate for coffee-equipment service and DSD, but it appears to have closed a take-private transaction on May 5, 2026, so it is excluded from the current US-listed candidate list. Layer 1B expansion for the restaurant equipment/service node produced one obvious reference equipment name and three underfollowed or speculative-shadow candidates tied to beverage equipment, coffee-service infrastructure, and refrigeration/regulatory service inputs. Evidence is strongest for Farmer Brothers because the provided external context explicitly mentions foodservice customers and coffee-machine service. Westrock Coffee is relevant as a B2B coffee/beverage supply-chain partner but equipment-service exposure is not yet proven. Middleby is the clearest reference equipment anchor, while Hudson Technologies is a second-order regulated-input hypothesis for refrigeration uptime rather than a restaurant-pure company. No buy/sell recommendation
